analysis.one_liner: Cipla makes and sells generic and branded medicines - respiratory, chronic-disease and specialty drugs mainly - across India, the US, South Africa and other markets.
analysis.whats_happening: Cipla reported Q2 FY27 (quarter ended Sep 30, 2026) results on October 27, 2026: revenue was roughly flat to slightly down (-2.4% YoY) at ₹7,404 crore, but EBITDA margin fell sharply to 18.7% from 25.0% a year ago, and consolidated net profit dropped by roughly a third. India sales hit a record high (+12% YoY), while US revenue was hurt by a supply disruption in lanreotide at manufacturing partner Pharmathen, which management does not expect to resolve this fiscal year. Management reiterated FY27 guidance of 18.5-20% EBITDA margin and a $1 billion annualised US exit run-rate, to be driven by new launches (Ventolin, generic Advair, plus three more pending launches).
analysis.plain_terms: Cipla sells medicines in India and abroad, and its India business is doing very well - its best quarter ever. But the company also depends on the US market for higher-margin products, and one of those products (lanreotide) is temporarily unavailable because of a manufacturing problem at a partner plant. That's why profit fell by about a third even though revenue barely moved - this is a margin story, not a sales collapse. The bigger question is whether new US product launches can replace what was lost.
analysis.quarters: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin improved 200 bps sequentially from Q1 FY27 but is still 630 bps lower than Q2 FY26 (18.7% vs 25.0%), so the margin reset is not yet reversed even though management says the trend is improving quarter on quarter. Reported net profit differs slightly by source - ₹851.51 crore per the company's own release reported by Free Press Journal versus ₹878 crore cited elsewhere - both point to a decline of roughly 35-37% YoY; treat the exact figure as directionally correct rather than precise to the rupee. North America revenue was $172 million, up $10 million sequentially, but down about 19% YoY in rupee terms because of the lanreotide disruption. Management guided FY27 EBITDA margin to 18.5-20% and effective tax rate to 27-27.5%.
analysis.performance_read: Over 1 year Cipla is down 9.6%, roughly tracking the Nifty (-10.9%) but far behind peer Dr Reddy's (+13.2%); the gap widens over 3 months and 3 years, where Cipla has underperformed both the index and the peer. Over 5 years Cipla has done well (+58% vs Nifty's +28.6% and the peer's +45.5%). There is no recent stock split, bonus or demerger in the supplied data (last split was in 2006), so the 16.3% fall from the October 2025 peak is a genuine price decline tied to the margin compression and regulatory issues described above, not a corporate-action artifact.
analysis.valuation_read: Cipla trades around 31-35x trailing earnings depending on the exact date and data source, close to the pharma industry median of roughly 31.9x. That is not statistically cheap or expensive versus peers - why it sits there is that the market is still pricing in the India franchise's strength and the promised US respiratory/peptide launches reaching a $1 billion run-rate; whether that premium is deserved depends on whether those launches arrive on schedule and whether the Pithampur plant's regulatory overhang gets resolved, neither of which is guaranteed.
analysis.growth_read: Growth is split by geography. India grew 12% YoY to a record quarter - that is volume/prescription-led growth, the healthier kind. But the consolidated business actually shrank slightly (-2.4% revenue) and margins fell sharply because of the US lanreotide disruption, so at the group level this quarter was neither margin-led nor volume-led growth - it was a loss of a high-margin product category that masked the India strength.
analysis.health_read: Cipla ended FY26 (March 2026) with a net cash position of about ₹10,526 crore against total debt of just ₹614 crore (mostly lease liabilities), so it is effectively debt-free. The business converts profit into cash comfortably; the real risk here is not financial (leverage) but operational/regulatory - a third-party manufacturing disruption that took out a US product, and an ongoing USFDA warning letter at the Pithampur (Indore) facility since November 2023, with a follow-up inspection in August 2026 still flagging seven observations.
analysis.ownership_read: Promoters (the Hamied family, led by Yusuf Khwaja Hamied at 18.69%) held 29.21% as of September 2026 with zero pledged shares - a clean promoter holding. Institutional ownership is broad: FIIs ~20.25%, mutual funds ~20.78%, insurers ~11.69%. Not verified - could not confirm from available sources whether any individually tracked marquee investor holds a stake; treat any such claim as unconfirmed rather than assume absence.
strengths: Net cash of roughly ₹10,526 crore against only ₹614 crore of debt (mostly leases) as of FY26-end - effectively debt-free
India business posted its highest-ever quarterly revenue in Q2 FY27, up 12% YoY
Zero promoter pledge on a 29.21% promoter holding as of September 2026
A separate US-facing Cipla facility passed an FDA inspection with zero observations on October 23, 2026
watchpoints: EBITDA margin fell from 25.0% to 18.7% YoY in Q2 FY27 - a 630 bps compression
US revenue fell about 19% YoY (in rupees) after a lanreotide supply disruption at manufacturing partner Pharmathen, which management says will not be resolved within FY27

The Pithampur (Indore) plant remains under a USFDA warning letter issued in November 2023; an August 2026 follow-up inspection resulted in a Form 483 with seven observations, which blocks new product approvals from that site
Consolidated net profit fell roughly 35-37% YoY in Q2 FY27 (reported as ₹851.51 crore or ₹878 crore depending on source) - the margin reset has not yet reversed despite management's guidance
analysis.one_thing: Whether Cipla's pipeline of new US launches (Ventolin, generic Advair, and three more pending launches) actually delivers the guided $1 billion annualised exit run-rate by the end of FY27, and whether the Pithampur plant clears its FDA warning letter, will show whether this margin reset is temporary or structural.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 revenue (₹7,404 crore) and EBITDA margin (18.7%) were consistent across multiple sources. Reported net profit varied between sources (₹851.51 crore vs ₹878 crore) - both imply a ~35-37% YoY decline, but the exact rupee figure is not fully reconciled here. Net cash/debt figures are from the FY26 (March 2026) annual results. Promoter holding and pledge data are from September 2026 shareholding-pattern trackers (Trendlyne, MarketsMojo) rather than a direct BSE/NSE filing check. Presence of any marquee individual investor on the register could not be verified.
